evidence: Reviewer claimed zig-linux-x86_64-0.14.0.tar.xz would 404; the PR later pins ZIG_VERSION=0.14.0 with a SHA256 the agent verified against the live asset (F11-F13 reply) and release-validate went green end-to-end (F9 reply 2), so the os-arch filename was correct for 0.14.0. The reply-hint says accept but the reply is a pushback.

Agent confirmed scripts/install.sh still rejected darwin/amd64 as 'not in the release matrix' and removed the guard; re-enabling the build target without the installer would have shipped an artifact the official installer refuses.
guidance_note: When re-enabling a platform in the build matrix, grep the repo for every guard and message that names that platform as unsupported (installer, docs, release globs) and update them in the same commit.

evidence: The '$8 = extra_cppflags ... appended to CPPFLAGS' doc line is in the original icu-cross-build.sh change, and 7f809ae touched only Dockerfile.release, so the ON-POST-REVIEW flag is a false positive. The doc said 'appended' while the code assigns CPPFLAGS outright; the fix kept a WHAT-comment and corrected it, so the why-only law was not what the fix applied.
guidance_note: When writing an argument doc for a shell script, read the line that consumes the argument and describe that exact operation (assign vs append).

evidence: The stale goreleaser-cross/osxcross description above the rewritten CC comment dates from the original toolchain swap; 7f809ae changed only Dockerfile.release, so the flag is a false positive. Agent rewrote only the build-stanza block, which left the file header stale (F10/F14).
guidance_note: When replacing a toolchain, grep the whole repo for the old toolchain's names (goreleaser-cross, osxcross, mingw) and rewrite every hit, including file headers, workflow headers and RELEASING.md, before the first push.

evidence: e759099 added the :ro GOMODCACHE mount with a comment claiming 'GOMODCACHE is populated by actions/setup-go', but setup-go only restores a cache and runs no go command, so a cold cache leaves the read-only mount empty. e759099 was an agent-initiated optimization, not a fix for any finding, so caused_by is null. The fix adds go mod download before docker run.
guidance_note: Before mounting a cache read-only, add the step that populates it, or confirm by name that an earlier step writes it; setup-go's cache:true only restores.

evidence: This is the same :ro mount defect as F5, in release.yml, where a cold-cache tag build would fail. The mount came from the agent's own e759099 optimization, not a finding fix. The fix is the same go mod download step.

This duplicates F6, re-raised in round 4 because the mount was still unaddressed: round 4 ran at 17:35 and the replies came at 17:50. 12618cf only relocated the tzfile/libresolv stubs and did not touch workflows, so the flag is a false positive.
This duplicates F5, re-raised in round 4 before the agent had replied. 12618cf did not touch release-validate.yml.

The hand-written TBD listed bare C names (res_init, dn_expand), not Mach-O _-prefixed/res_9_ symbols. The agent agreed in principle and then deleted the stub, vendoring a pinned MacOSX 13.3 SDK whose real libresolv.tbd resolves -lresolv (0ca6f5b). 12618cf only moved the stub from an inline printf to a file, so the logic is relocated, not fix-caused.
guidance_note: When a cross-link needs an Apple system library or framework, vendor the real SDK's .tbd/Frameworks rather than hand-writing a symbol export list.

evidence: 1c6c5fe, the named fix for F4, rewrote the build-stanza comment but left the .goreleaser.yml file header describing goreleaser-cross:v1.26.2-3 + osxcross/mingw/glibc. The agent admitted 'I had updated the build-stanza comment but missed the file-header block'.
guidance_note: When fixing a stale-description finding, grep the file and repo for the stale term and fix every hit, not just the one the reviewer anchored on.

evidence: The goreleaser curl|tar with no digest check is in the round-0 diff hunk, so it predates 0ca6f5b and the flag is a false positive. The agent pinned SHA256 and verified with sha256sum -c for all four downloaded inputs.
guidance_note: When a Dockerfile downloads toolchain binaries that build release artifacts, pin a SHA256 per version and verify it before extraction in the original change.

evidence: The unverified zig download is in the original round-0 diff, not 0ca6f5b. The fix was swept across all four downloads in d05b92e.

The macOS SDK curl|tar was introduced in 0ca6f5b, the change that resolved F9 by vendoring the SDK. It copied the PR's existing unverified-download pattern, so the fix added a new unpinned third-party input. The post-extract test -d checks prove only the archive's shape.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a new third-party download, give it the same integrity pinning a release input needs, rather than copying the neighbouring unverified pattern.

evidence: This re-raises F10 in round 7 (20:24), before the agent's 20:32 fix. It is the same stale .goreleaser.yml header that F4's fix (1c6c5fe) missed. 0ca6f5b did not touch .goreleaser.yml.

The base is golang:${GO_VERSION}-bookworm plus direct HTTPS downloads, so packages: read is dead. b61fb38 even rewrote its comment to 'pull base images from ghcr', which is false. b61fb38 was an agent-initiated smoke/validate split, not a finding fix, so caused_by is null; the dead scope dates from the original toolchain swap.
guidance_note: When removing a GHCR base image, drop the packages scope it justified in every workflow, rather than rewording the comment that justifies it.

evidence: The release.yml opening summary still said goreleaser-cross after F10's fix claimed 'one description of the toolchain contract'. Neither the F4 nor the F10 fix swept the term repo-wide, and cd18487 touched release.yml permissions without fixing its header.
guidance_note: After a toolchain swap, run one repo-wide grep for the old name and treat a non-empty result as an unfinished fix.

evidence: HTTPInstaller rejects non-.tar.gz URLs, and this PR publishes the windows .zip (glob in the round-0 diff, not cd18487), so windows downgrade resolves an asset it cannot install. The agent corrected the installer comment that said .zip 'would only appear if windows builds came back' and gave a clearer error (458b784). It tracked zip extraction as links-downgrade-t244.8, a defensible scope split.
guidance_note: When publishing a new archive format, grep the consumers of the release manifest (installer, downgrade) for extension checks before adding the publish glob.

evidence: RELEASING.md:65-68 still named goreleaser-cross:v1.26.2-3/osxcross/glibc. It is the same stale-toolchain-description gap the F4 and F10 fixes did not sweep, now in operator docs.
guidance_note: Include docs (RELEASING.md, README) in the old-name grep after changing the build substrate.

evidence: RELEASING.md:50-56 still said release-validate runs on every PR and gates merge. b61fb38 removed the pull_request trigger; it was an agent-initiated change, not a finding fix, so caused_by is null, but the drift is the agent's own.
guidance_note: When changing a workflow's triggers, grep docs for the workflow's filename and update every description of when it runs in the same commit.

narrative: A toolchain swap from goreleaser-cross to zig, iterated through many CI-fixing pushes, each of which drew a fresh review round. The dominant cost was stale descriptions of the old toolchain: F4, F10, F14, F16 and F18 are one gap found one file at a time, because each fix patched only the anchored comment. The agent's pushback on F1 was correct, and its handling of F9 was strong: it replaced a hand-written TBD with the real SDK. Several flagged findings (F5-F8, F15, F19) came from the agent's own unrequested mid-review changes, not from finding fixes.
guidance_observations: A single repo-wide grep for the replaced toolchain's names after the first stale-comment finding would have removed four later findings and at least two rounds.
Pushing exploratory CI fixes onto a PR under automated review spends a review round per push; iterate on a scratch branch or workflow_dispatch until green, then push.
Mid-review optimizations (the GOMODCACHE :ro mount, the trigger split) introduced their own findings; unrequested scope added during review needs the same pre-push sweep as the original change.

evidence: loadBlocksEdges had no ORDER BY, so adjacency order, and therefore the DFS cycle path, depended on row order, while the code claimed determinism. The fix added ORDER BY r.src_id, r.dst_id (cd24c82).
guidance_note: When a comment claims deterministic output, trace every input order feeding it back to its source query and confirm each one is sorted.

evidence: DependencyCycle was assigned liveBlocksCycle's nil when there was no cycle, so it encoded as null while Errors/Warnings are initialized to empty slices. The field is from the original commit; cd24c82 only added ORDER BY, so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: When adding a slice field to a JSON report struct, initialize it the same way its sibling slice fields are initialized.

evidence: The message 'blocks: <dependency> already depends on <dependent>' never names the edge being rejected. The agent rephrased it to lead with the attempted direction. The message is original code untouched by cd24c82. The reply-hint says pushback, but the agent accepted.

narrative: This PR prevents and diagnoses blocks-dependency cycles. All three findings were real and pre-existing in the original commit: a nondeterministic cycle path, a null JSON field, and an unclear error message. Each was fixed directly, and no finding arose from a fix.
guidance_observations: Matching new struct fields to sibling conventions (empty slices, not nil) is a mechanical pre-push check that would have avoided F2.

evidence: DeleteComment returned fmt.Errorf('comment %q not found') while GetIssue and the relation removals return the typed NotFoundError. Switching to NotFoundError keeps the message and enables errors.As.
guidance_note: When adding a new store mutation, copy the not-found error type from the nearest sibling mutation rather than writing a fresh fmt.Errorf.

evidence: The unchecked DELETE is in the original commit; f4c1737 changed only the not-found return, so the flag is a false positive. The agent's claim that one transaction makes 'found it but deleted nothing' unrepresentable holds only if withMutation serializes writers or the SELECT locks the row. The packet shows neither the isolation level nor withMutation's locking, so the pushback is unverified, and no-defensive-null-guards does not cover a RowsAffected check.
guidance_note: Before pushing back on a concurrency premise by appeal to the transaction, name the isolation or locking mechanism that makes the race impossible and point at it.

narrative: This PR adds comment deletion. F1 (typed not-found error) was a correct consistency fix. F2 (no RowsAffected check after DELETE) drew a reasoned pushback resting on a transactional-isolation claim the packet cannot confirm. Neither finding was caused by a fix.
guidance_observations: A pushback that relies on transaction semantics should cite the mechanism (isolation level, row lock, workspace mutex); the reply asserted unrepresentability without showing it.

evidence: runLifeboatDump's usage string advertised [--json] but registered no local --json flag, so 'lit lifeboat dump --json' fails flag parsing. The agent took the reviewer's first option and dropped [--json], matching lit export.
guidance_note: When writing a usage string, list only flags the flag set actually registers; copy the usage shape of the command being mirrored (lit export).

narrative: This PR adds the raw dump reader and the lifeboat dump command. One real usage-string defect was fixed cleanly, and the second round was clean.

evidence: cellTimePtr returned nil for a non-empty unparseable timestamp, silently zeroing recovery data. 4a57173 added TransformTimestamp, which errors with table/column context. The fix kept Transform as a per-mapping field, which left the identity-on-timestamp path that F5 found.
guidance_note: When moving a validation into a transform, ask what happens when a mapping selects a different transform for the same field, and make that combination unrepresentable.

evidence: Validate's 'mapped, ok := disp.(MappedTo); if !ok { continue }' let nil or any other disposition pass as a drop. This is original code; 4a57173 did not touch Validate's switch, so the flag is a false positive. The fix made the type switch exhaustive with a default reject.
guidance_note: When writing a trust-boundary validator over an interface-typed value, use an exhaustive type switch with a rejecting default from the start.

evidence: scanMigrationDrops fed whole migration files, including the goose Down section, to parseDroppedColumns, so a Down DROP COLUMN would count as an intended drop. This is original code untouched by 7771b2d. The agent reused the existing gooseUpSection helper. The defect is a parsing-scope bug, not a duplicated source of truth.
guidance_note: When parsing goose migrations for history, reuse the existing gooseUpSection helper that other parsers in the package already use.

evidence: tableTarget allowed two columns (prompt and agent_prompt, both aliases in knownSourceColumns) to resolve to issues.prompt, and the later cell overwrote the earlier. This is original code; 667d86d only changed the Up-section scan, so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: When a correspondence table maps aliases onto one target, add the duplicate-target rejection in the same change as the aliases.

evidence: F1's fix (4a57173) changed cellTime to read only an already-parsed time.Time, so a timestamp target mapped via identity now silently becomes time.Time{}. Before that fix it would have been parsed. Rather than add a compatibility check, the agent moved the transform onto the target registry and removed it from MappedTo (d66f4dd), making the mismatch unrepresentable.
guidance_note: When a fix makes a downstream reader trust an upstream conversion, check every path that can skip that conversion before pushing.

evidence: The single-collection invariant existed in the original tableTarget; d66f4dd only relocated it into Validate, so the flag is a false positive. The agent agreed issue_history cannot be represented but deferred it to links-recovery-j0vl.6, noting DeterministicMap declines the table so the result is a loud failure, not silent loss. It took three replies to settle the ticket id.
guidance_note: Look up a follow-up ticket's id before posting it, so the thread needs no correction replies.

evidence: An issues table with only id passed DeterministicMap and Validate, and Apply fabricated empty fields. This is original code; d66f4dd did not add it. The agent gated issues only and claimed thin non-issues tables 'fail loudly at the write path', which it later admitted was wrong (F10 reply 1), so the fix seeded F10-F12.
guidance_note: Before scoping a fix to one table because the others 'fail loudly', read the write path (ReplaceFromExport) and confirm it actually runs the required-field checks.

evidence: 55e4fa6, the commit carrying F7's hasRequiredColumns gate, shows the canonicalEventReason comment changing from '' to a lone curly quote, alongside gofmt-style list re-indentation in the same file. The agent's claim that this was 'a pre-existing typo just outside this PR's diff' is contradicted by that diff. The reply-hint says pushback, but the agent fixed it.
guidance_note: Review the full diff of a fix commit for incidental formatter rewrites (gofmt doc-comment normalization turns '' into a curly quote) before pushing.

evidence: dropColumnRE matched one DROP COLUMN per ALTER TABLE, so 'DROP COLUMN a, DROP COLUMN b' captured only a. This is original code untouched by 55e4fa6. The fix was a two-level parse with a multi-drop test (f9774af).
guidance_note: When writing a regex extractor documented as returning 'every' match, test it with a statement containing two matches.

evidence: F7's fix gated only issues, while comments(issue_id) still passed and ReplaceFromExport's raw INSERTs fabricated an empty comment. The agent conceded 'my earlier ... fail loudly at the write path was wrong' and generalized the gate to required-target coverage for every domain table.
guidance_note: When a reviewer gives one table as the example of a shape gap, apply the fix to every table the same code path handles.

evidence: F10's fix (e1f20d9) introduced a hand-maintained requiredTargets list that omitted id/title/created_at/created_by/reason/actor, so thin tables still passed. The agent recognized 'three rounds of the gate is still too thin' and moved requiredness onto the target registry (f1348b2).
guidance_note: When gating on required fields, derive requiredness from the single place the fields are defined in the first fix, never from a parallel hand list.

evidence: f1348b2 (F11's fix) kept the coverage check in DeterministicMap, so an LLM-supplied partial mapping still passed Validate, the documented trust boundary. The agent moved the check into tableShapeProblems in Validate (3d475c2) and removed the duplicate.
guidance_note: Put a new invariant in the documented trust boundary (Validate), not in one producer, the first time it is added.

evidence: Apply indexes row[mc.index] while Validate never checked row arity, so a short row panics. The indexing is original Apply code; 3d475c2 changed only the coverage check, so the flag is a false positive. The fix added the arity check to Validate.
guidance_note: When a validator guards positional indexing, list every precondition the indexer relies on (column coverage and row length) and check each one.

narrative: The ShapeMapping contract took 11 rounds. Many findings were genuine original gaps in a trust-boundary design (non-exhaustive switch, goose Down scan, duplicate targets, row arity). The costly chain was the recognizable-shape gate: an issues-only gate based on a wrong write-path claim (F7), then a hand list (F10), then registry-derived requiredness in the wrong layer (F11), then the move into Validate (F12). That chain cost three rounds that a registry-derived check in Validate on the first fix would have avoided. The F7 fix commit also let a formatter mangle an unrelated comment (F8), which the agent then misattributed as pre-existing.
guidance_observations: The agent named the anti-pattern only on the third 'still too thin' round; recognizing a hand-maintained required list as a parallel source of truth should happen on the first fix.

Several replies made checkable factual claims (thin tables 'fail loudly at the write path', the curly quote was 'pre-existing') that the code or the commit diff contradicted; verify such claims before posting them.

evidence: Discard returned early on store == nil, so a failed RemoveAll could never be retried. The fix releases store and root against their own state and clears root only on success, and it also nested the workspace under root so lock and snapshot siblings are inside the owned tree. The reply says the test holds the dir open; the test actually uses chmod.
guidance_note: When one method releases two resources, track each resource's held state separately from the start.

evidence: The compile claim is wrong: Go's os.Geteuid exists on Windows and returns -1. The test F1's fix added (4199116) is still POSIX-only at runtime, because chmod 0o555 on a directory does not block unlinking on Windows. The agent accepted on that real ground, but repeated the compile premise without checking it.
guidance_note: When a test injects failure through POSIX permission bits, put it behind //go:build !windows in the commit that adds it.

evidence: 4199116, F1's fix, deleted 'defer cand.Discard()' in TestRebuildCandidateRejectLeavesZeroResidue and replaced it with an explicit Discard at the end. That opened a leak window when Export or the count assertion calls Fatalf. The fix added t.Cleanup in every candidate test.
guidance_note: When replacing a defer with an explicit call so the call can be asserted, keep a t.Cleanup alongside it for early-exit paths.

evidence: F3's fix (3bfb26a) swept t.Cleanup for Discard across all candidate tests but missed the other early-exit-sensitive state in TestDiscardRetriesDirectoryRemoval: the parent chmod 0o555, which strands the TempDir unwritable if the test exits early. The fix registered a t.Cleanup restore right after the chmod.
guidance_note: When sweeping a cleanup pattern for one resource, also list every other piece of mutated test state (permissions, env, cwd) in the same tests and give each its own cleanup.

narrative: This PR adds the throwaway-candidate lifecycle. F1 was a real retry bug, and the fix was structurally good, including bringing Open's sibling artifacts inside the owned root. Every later finding came from the F1 fix's test changes: a POSIX-only test without a build tag, a removed defer that opened a leak window, and a chmod with no cleanup. Two rounds were spent on test hygiene of the fix itself.
guidance_observations: The fix commit's new test was the source of every follow-up finding; review the fix's own tests for early-exit cleanup and platform portability before pushing.
The agent accepted F2's false compile premise without checking it; the change survived only because a separate, real rationale existed.
